tldr: Most of this thread shares a "Same X, Different Y" title pattern, not one event. Three arXiv papers (Oct 22-26) cover chemistry identifier binding, credit assignment for agentic RL and news framing; a Nov 1 post then reported a 17-point gap between agents using one model.
whats_new: On Nov 3, an IBM Research Hugging Face post compared CUGA, Hermes and Deep Agents on the same model, asking when to pick CUGA.
why_it_matters: Two harness-versus-model posts in three days make the same point: the agent harness can move results as much as the model, so evaluate the full stack.

status.detail: Title-match papers are coincidental; the Nov 1 and Nov 3 posts form the real thread on harness effects.

beats.headline: Two arXiv papers on reliability and agentic RL
beats.summary: Identifier binding failures in chemistry LLMs, and twin-world credit assignment for agentic RL.

beats.headline: A multi-agent system compares news framing across outlets
beats.summary: A research prototype for news analysis, loosely related.

beats.headline: Same model, different agent: 17 points apart on 21 MCP servers
beats.summary: A practitioner post on agent-level variance with a fixed model.

beats.headline: IBM Research compares CUGA, Hermes and Deep Agents on one model
beats.summary: A vendor harness comparison on Hugging Face.

open_questions: Does the MCP post publish its harness differences, prompts and scoring method so the 17-point gap can be reproduced?
Does the IBM CUGA post report numbers on a shared benchmark, and can they be rerun?
Do any of the arXiv papers release code or evals that apply to tool-using agents?
take_for_builders: Hold the model fixed and vary the harness in your own eval on your MCP servers; treat the 17-point figure and IBM's CUGA comparison as vendor or blog results until reproduced.
